title: Pinsker's inequality under absolute continuity
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$, and write $\mathrm{TV}(\mu,
u)$ for their total variation distance. Suppose $\mu$ is absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$, and that the log-likelihood ratio $x \mapsto \log rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)$ is $\mu$-integrable. Then
\[
  2\,\mathrm{TV}(\mu,
u)^2 \;\le\; \int_\Omega \log rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)\,d\mu(x),
\]
the right-hand side being the Kullback–Leibler divergence of $\mu$ from $
u$.
hypotheses_covered: μ, ν are probability measures on a measurable space Ω
μ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν
the log-likelihood ratio log(dμ/dν) is μ-integrable
